95.notes: RetroZilla 2.3 by rn10950 (unofficial, open source, GitHub release 2025-06-11), a Gecko 1.8.1 (SeaMonkey/Firefox 2 era) browser suite whose README lists Windows 95, 98, Me, NT 3.51 and NT 4.0. Release notes: NSS updated with TLS 1.3 support, updated certificate store. This is the only maintained TLS-capable browser for 9x found; it renders like Firefox 2, so many JavaScript-heavy sites (e.g. Google results) do not work, and MSAA/screen-reader support is that of old Gecko (not verified). NOT HASHED: the downloaded installer (13410304 bytes, the size GitHub reports) was detected and quarantined by Microsoft Defender on the host as Trojan:Win32/Pomal!rfn (a reputation/ML detection, possibly a false positive, not investigated); it was not restored. Size from the GitHub API; sha256/signer must be filled in only after the detection is resolved. Installer silent switches not documented. A zip build retrozilla-2.3.en-US.win32.zip (12677968 bytes) is in the same release. read 2026-11-25

Playing in the Dark (author of the free Top Speed audio racing games) still lists the old Top Speed 1.1a and 2.00 on https://www.playinginthedark.net/download/, but the files (playinginthedark.net/downloads/Tspeed_1.1a.exe, Tspeed_2.00.exe; the page also points at dead users.pandora.be links) return HTTP 404 now, and the page states no OS requirements. Top Speed 3 (XP entry) is built with VS2008 and is not expected to run on 9x. GMA Games titles (e.g. Shades of Doom) are commercial. No free audio game with a stated 9x requirement found on an author's page. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Unofficial Windows ME Service Pack 1 2.02 Beta 9
me.name_pl: Nieoficjalny Service Pack 1 2.02 Beta 9 dla Windows ME
me.notes: Unofficial Windows ME Service Pack 1 2.02 Beta 9 (English), MSFN topic 61407, distributed from MDGx (file dated 2007-10-01, 20.9 MB, HEAD Content-Length 21935104). MDGx labels it OLD; it is a beta and unmaintained. Installs previously released hotfixes. No silent switches documented. NOT DOWNLOADED, NOT HASHED: www.mdgx.com answered HTTP 200 to a browser-style HEAD request but HTTP 403 to the scripted download; no browser-identity workaround was used. Size, hash and signer must be filled in after a manual download (MDGx publishes no hashes). read 2026-11-25

me.name: Unofficial Windows ME Service Pack 2 Alpha 2
me.name_pl: Nieoficjalny Service Pack 2 Alpha 2 dla Windows ME
me.notes: Withdrawn by its author: MDGx states "ME SP2 is temporarily OFFline due to untested BUGs per author's request" (project thread winprj.net t=781); /spx/MESP2.EXE is disabled and only /spx/MESP2_BUGGY!.EXE (6.33 MB, "try it anyway at your own risk", needs IE 6 SP1) is offered. Not recorded because the author withdrew it. read 2026-11-25

me.name: KernelEx 4.5.2
me.notes: KernelEx 4.5.2 by Xeno86 (unofficial, GPLv2, SourceForge project kernelex, released 2011; last release, project dormant). Adds missing NT-era kernel32/user32/shell32 APIs so some newer programs (e.g. Firefox up to 8) run on Windows 98/98 SE/ME; not for Windows 95. 4.5.2 adds the VKrnlEx.vxd in-memory patch (no on-disk kernel32 change). URL is the project's SourceForge download redirect; MD5 e5f833acc4a69085e86097a1f2346e92 matches the MD5 SourceForge publishes in the project RSS. No silent switches documented. Not Authenticode-signed (signer empty). read 2026-11-25

me.name: Security update KB918547 (MS06-026, Graphics Rendering Engine/WMF)
me.signer: CN=Microsoft Corporation, O=Microsoft Corporation, L=Redmond, S=Washington, C=US
me.notes: Official Microsoft critical update from bulletin MS06-026 (June 2006, the WMF/GDI fix for 98/98 SE/ME that was issued only through Windows Update; GDI32.DLL/GDI.EXE 4.90.3003). Still served by Microsoft from the Windows Update cabpool over HTTP only (the file link is the one MDGx lists), so verify by hash. Windows ME package. MDGx notes it supersedes the older GDI fixes. Microsoft documents no silent switches for it here. Authenticode signature valid (Microsoft Corporation). Extended support for 98/ME ended 2006-07-11. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Security update KB891711 v2 (cursor and icon handling)
me.name_pl: Aktualizacja zabezpieczeń KB891711 v2 (obsługa kursorów i ikon)
me.signer: CN=Microsoft Corporation, O=Microsoft Corporation, L=Redmond, S=Washington, C=US
me.notes: Official Microsoft update KB891711 version 2 for the cursor and icon format handling vulnerability (MS05-002 era, Windows Update only for 9x). Served by Microsoft from the Windows Update cabpool over HTTP only; verify by hash. Windows ME package. No silent switches documented. Authenticode signature valid (Microsoft Corporation). read 2026-11-25

me.name: Security update Q329115 (SSL certificate validation, CRYPT32)
me.name_pl: Aktualizacja zabezpieczeń Q329115 (weryfikacja certyfikatów SSL, CRYPT32)
me.signer: CN=Microsoft Corporation, OU=Copyright (c) 2002 Microsoft Corp., O=Microsoft Corporation, L=Redmond, S=Washington, C=US
me.notes: Official Microsoft Windows ME fix Q329115 for the SSL certificate chain identity spoofing flaw (CRYPT32.DLL + CRYPTDLG.DLL, MS02-050 era). Served by the Windows Update cabpool over HTTP only (link as listed by MDGx); verify by hash. Does not add modern TLS. No silent switches documented. Authenticode signature valid (Microsoft Corporation, 2002). read 2026-11-25

me.name: RetroZilla 2.3 (browser with TLS 1.3)
me.notes: RetroZilla 2.3 by rn10950 (unofficial, open source, GitHub release 2025-06-11), a Gecko 1.8.1 (SeaMonkey/Firefox 2 era) browser suite whose README lists Windows 95, 98, Me, NT 3.51 and NT 4.0. Release notes: NSS updated with TLS 1.3 support, updated certificate store. This is the only maintained TLS-capable browser for 9x found; it renders like Firefox 2, so many JavaScript-heavy sites (e.g. Google results) do not work, and MSAA/screen-reader support is that of old Gecko (not verified). NOT HASHED: the downloaded installer (13410304 bytes, the size GitHub reports) was detected and quarantined by Microsoft Defender on the host as Trojan:Win32/Pomal!rfn (a reputation/ML detection, possibly a false positive, not investigated); it was not restored. Size from the GitHub API; sha256/signer must be filled in only after the detection is resolved. Installer silent switches not documented. A zip build retrozilla-2.3.en-US.win32.zip (12677968 bytes) is in the same release. read 2026-11-25

me.name: DirectX 9.0c end-user runtime (last for 98/ME)
me.notes: Not available officially. Microsoft (DirectX SDK team, Chuck Walbourn) states the last DirectX End-User Runtime supporting Windows 98/ME was October 2006 and that it is no longer available; December 2006 and later D3DX9 are not compatible with 98/ME. The Download Center pages for the 2006 redists (details id=353 Dec 2006, id=20265 Aug 2006) now return 404; the June 2010 runtime (id=8109) lists only XP SP2 and later. Copies exist only on third-party sites and archive.org, not recorded. Fredledingue's page on htasoft.com hosts a community-provided dx90c.exe (origin and signature not checked, not recorded). read 2026-11-25

me.name: .NET Framework 2.0 (RTM, last for 98/ME)
me.notes: Not available officially. The 2.0 RTM redistributable dotnetfx.exe (download.microsoft.com/download/5/6/7/567758a3-759e-473e-bf8f-52154438565a/dotnetfx.exe) returns 404, its Download Center FamilyID 0856EACB-4362-4B0D-8EDD-AAB15C5E04F5 goes to the 404 page. The still-listed 2.0 SP1 (details id=16614, NetFx20SP1_x86.exe) does not support Windows 98/ME (SP1 dropped 9x). Requires IE 5.01+ and Windows Installer 2.0 on 98/ME. Only third-party/archive.org copies remain, not recorded. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Visual C++ 2005 SP1 redistributable (x86)
me.notes: Not available for this system. The original SP1 redist (8.0.50727.762, download/e/1/c/e1c773de-.../vcredist_x86.exe) and the RTM redist return 404. The only listed package, the MFC security update 8.0.50727.6195 (details id=26347, vcredist_x86.EXE 2710520 bytes), names supported OS: Windows XP, Server 2003, Vista, Server 2008/R2, 7 only; no Windows 98/ME statement, so it is not recorded for Windows ME. VC++ 2005 is the last compiler whose CRT targets 9x, but no official 9x-supported redist download remains. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Visual Basic 6.0 SP6 run-time (vbrun60sp6.exe)
me.notes: Not available officially. Microsoft's VB6 downloads page still links "Service Pack 6 for Visual Basic 6.0: Run-Time Redistribution Pack" (FamilyID 7b9ba261-7a9c-43e7-9117-f673077ffb3c), but it now redirects to the Download Center 404 page, and the old direct file VB6.0-KB290887-X86.exe returns 404. The VB6 SP6 Cumulative Update MSI (details id=7030, KB2708437) lists only Windows 2000/XP/2003/Vista/2008. MDGx hosts an unofficial MSVBVM60.DLL 6.0.9821 repack (not recorded); most VB6 programs ship their own runtime files. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Windows Installer 2.0 for Windows 9x (InstMsiA.exe)
me.notes: Not available officially. download.microsoft.com/download/WindowsInstaller/Install/2.0/W9XMe/EN-US/InstMsiA.exe and its FamilyID cebbacd8-c094-4255-b702-de3bb768148f return 404 / the 404 page. Needed only by MSI-based installers; none of the downloadable entries here need it. Windows ME ships Windows Installer 1.2 in the box. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Internet Explorer 6 SP1 (last for 98/ME)
me.notes: Not available officially. The web installer download.microsoft.com/download/ie6sp1/finrel/6_sp1/W98NT42KMeXP/EN-US/ie6setup.exe returns 404 (and its component servers are gone). IE6 has no TLS 1.2, so it is useless on the modern web anyway; use RetroZilla or the hypervisor HTTPS proxy. Full offline copies exist only on third-party/archive.org sites, not recorded. Note: .NET 2.0 and the ME/98 hotfixes assume IE 5.01+ already present. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Microsoft Layer for Unicode (unicows.dll)
me.notes: Not available officially. MDGx's link download.microsoft.com/download/b/7/5/b75eace3-00e2-4aa0-9a6f-0b6882c71642/unicows.exe and FamilyID 73BA7BD7-ED06-4F0D-80A4-2A7EEAEE17E2 return 404. Applications that need it ship their own unicows.dll; KernelEx can use it if present. read 2026-11-25

me.name: Anti-malware for Windows ME
me.notes: None found. No anti-malware vendor supports Windows 95/98/ME today: current pages of Microsoft, Avast, ESET and others start at Windows 7 or later, and the last 9x-capable products (e.g. ClamWin, old AVG/Avast versions) stopped receiving signature updates years ago. Charon must say there is no supported anti-malware for this system and keep the guest off the open network except through the hypervisor proxy. read 2026-11-25
